editorial:
Ever wonder what it was actually like to live as a peasant hundreds of years ago? You get a raw look at that in this film, which focuses on the massive uprising in 1381. It is not just a dry history lesson; it feels more like a gritty drama that shows you how bad things really were. You will see people treated like slaves by their own government, dealing with unfair taxes and bosses who did not care if they lived or died. The vibe is heavy and intense, making you feel the frustration of the poor people who finally decided they had enough and wanted to fight back against the rich.

What really works here is how the movie shows the clash between the lower class and the royal court. The acting is solid and makes the anger feel real, though the pacing can feel a bit slow in some spots since it is part documentary. If you enjoy learning about the dark side of history, you will love this. You can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you want a sharp picture, or you might want to rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you like owning rare historical gems.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a sad note. After the peasants march on London and demand their rights, the young King Richard II tricks them. He promises to help them and grant their freedom, but it is all a lie. Once the crowds go home, the government goes back on its word. The leaders of the revolt are captured and killed, and the poor people end up right back where they started, still trapped in a broken system.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and learning about social struggles.
